catalog_quote: p.158: "La place de l'accent est prévisible. En règle générale, l'accent porte sur la première syllabe de l'unité accentuelle, sauf lorsque celle-ci est un élément proclitique. La syllabe ha(n)-, la nasale syllabique Ń et une syllabe dont la voyelle [ə] est le noyau constituent des éléments clitiques. Leur présence implique que l'accent se porte sur la deuxième syllabe." ... p.166: "La place de celui-ci n'assume aucune fonction distinctive; l'accent occupe une place déterminée dans l'unité accentuelle: il frappe la première syllabe de l'élément accentogène, en l'occurrence le radical. De ce fait, il assure, outre sa fonction contrastive, une fonction démarcative."

new_statements.quote: p.159: "La place de l'accent est prévisible. En règle générale, l'accent porte sur la première syllabe de l'unité accentuelle, sauf lorsque celle-ci est un élément proclitique. La syllabe ha(n)-, la nasale syllabique [N] et une syllabe dont la voyelle [ə] est le noyau constituent des éléments clitiques. Leur présence implique que l'accent se porte sur la deuxième syllabe." p.160: "Autrement dit, l'accent frappe toujours la première syllabe de l'élément accentogène ou la deuxième syllabe de l'unité accentuelle lorsque la première est une syllabe proclitique" ... p.167: "La place de celui-ci n'assume aucune fonction distinctive ; l'accent occupe une place déterminée dans l'unité accentuelle : il frappe la première syllabe de l'élément accentogène, en l'occurrence le radical."
new_statements.translation: p.159: 'The place of the accent is predictable. As a general rule, the accent falls on the first syllable of the accentual unit, except when that syllable is a proclitic element. The syllable ha(n)-, the syllabic nasal and a syllable whose nucleus is the vowel [ə] are clitic elements. Their presence means the accent falls on the second syllable.' p.160: 'In other words, the accent always strikes the first syllable of the accent-bearing element, or the second syllable of the accentual unit when the first is a proclitic syllable.' p.167: 'Its place has no distinctive function; the accent occupies a fixed place in the accentual unit: it strikes the first syllable of the accent-bearing element, namely the radical.'

new_statements.relation_note: Language not in the catalog and no existing statements; this is the first opened source with a stress statement for bala1301. It supplies: stem-initial (root) stress, non-contrastive, penult echo/secondary accent in long units, and an explicit rejection of a tonal analysis. The thesis describes the soːfa sub-dialect of kantoːhe (= Kentohe), so it is about bala1301 proper.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word (accentual-unit) stress is predictable and non-contrastive: it falls on the first syllable of the stem/radical (the 'élément accentogène'); proclitic syllables such as the class prefix ha(n)-, a syllabic nasal or a schwa-nucleus prefix syllable are never stressed, so surface stress is on the first syllable unless a proclitic precedes, then on the second (e.g. ['biti] 'dog', [ha'la:nte] 'man', [kə'demat] 'tongue' vs ['demat] 'tongues'). Stress is realised as extra intensity and some extra pitch. The author also states (pp. 169-170) that tone could not be demonstrated: no minimal pairs, no H/L word melodies, no grammatical tone; the high pitch on the stressed stem-initial syllable is treated as a phonetic correlate of accent, so Balanta soːfa is analysed as a non-tonal stress language with demarcative (not distinctive) accent.
new_statements.secondary_stress: p.160: "Dans les unités accentuelles de plus de trois syllabes, on peut noter un écho d'accent assimilable à un accent secondaire (..) sur l'avant dernière syllabe." — in accentual units of more than three syllables an echo accent, comparable to a secondary stress, on the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: Proclitics (class prefix ha(n)-, syllabic nasal, schwa-nucleus syllables) are unstressable, shifting stress to the second syllable of the unit; the accentual unit may be a morpheme, syntheme or phrase (fn. 104) and never exceeds five syllables (p. ~220); accent has only contrastive/demarcative function, no distinctive function (pp. 167, 252); tonal 'bridge' raising between intonation groups is phonetic only (p. 170).
new_statements.identity_note: Mbodj 2011 describes the soːfa sub-dialect of the kantoːhe (Kentohe) dialect of Balanta, spoken north of the Geba river, Guinea-Bissau (thesis p. 16: 'Le dialecte kanto:he se subdivise en deux sous-dialectes : le sofa et le fac'); informants were checked to be representative kantoːhe speakers. This is Balanta-Kentohe (bala1301), not Balanta-Ganja (bala1302). de Sousa Bella 1946 (unopened) concerns the Balanta of Jabadá.

tone.quote: Dos trabalhos que apresentam algum esquema tonal, temos Wilson (1961a) para o kəntɔhɛ da Guiné-Bissau e N’Diaye-Corréard (1973) para o fca. Doneux (1984ː 23) faz alguns comentários importantes sobre o tom em balanta. Inicialmente, segundo o autor, não é preciso marcar os tons em balanta, salvo raras exceções, como, por exemplo, para diferenciar, o morfema de ‘1P’ e de ‘2P’, cuja forma de ‘2P’ é {bàa}; segundo, não se pode analisar o balanta em termos de acento, porque não há uma posição dentro da palavra que determine se há ou não uma altura; terceiro, o balanta é uma língua com colocação tonal obrigatória sobre os elementos morfológicos ou sintaticamante definidos
tone.locator: pp. 19-20, Introducao section 4.3 'A questao dos tons': heading and the author's own classification ('o sistema tonal, se existe, nao foi suficientemente analisado e, para nos, claramente o tom em balanta nao e lexical e, se ha tom, este e gramatical') on p. 19; the quoted passage (Wilson 1961a for kentohe.. Doneux 1984: 23..) and Quadro 3 on p. 20
tone.translation: Of the works that present some tonal scheme, we have Wilson (1961a) for the kəntɔhɛ of Guinea-Bissau and N'Diaye-Correard (1973) for fca. Doneux (1984: 23) makes some important comments on tone in Balanta. First, according to the author, it is not necessary to mark tones in Balanta, save rare exceptions, e.g. to differentiate the 1PL and 2PL morphemes, whose 2PL form is {baa} [low]; second, Balanta cannot be analysed in terms of accent, because there is no position within the word that determines whether or not there is a pitch [height]; third, Balanta is a language with obligatory tone placement on morphologically or syntactically defined elements
tone.says: Section 4.3 pp. 20-21: the author does not transcribe tone; 'the tonal system, if it exists, has not been sufficiently analysed; for us tone in Balanta is clearly not lexical and, if there is tone, it is grammatical'; older works mark diacritics, recent ones drop them, Biaye 2003/04 analyses (Ganja) in terms of accent/intensity not pitch; works giving a tonal scheme are Wilson 1961a for kentohe and N'Diaye-Correard 1973 for fca; Doneux 1984:23 (Kentohe) says tones need not be marked except rare…
